summary: Sets out routing requirements for home control and automation applications on low-power and lossy networks. It covers devices like sensors, actuators and controllers that have short radio range and rely on routing. It is informational.

eli5.summary: Many little gadgets in a house, like light switches and heaters, must pass messages along like a chain of neighbors, and this lists what that chain needs.

questions: what is a low power and lossy network
how many devices must a home automation routing protocol support
subtitle: What a routing protocol must do to connect light switches, sensors and heaters in a home.

tldr.problem: Homes are filling with small battery-powered and mains-powered wireless devices with a short radio range, so messages must be routed hop by hop over unreliable links.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC walks through home use cases and turns them into routing requirements for low-power and lossy networks: constraint-based routing, mobility, scalability, convergence time, manageability and stability.
tldr.outcome: It is an Informational requirements document. It sets targets such as supporting at least 250 devices and converging within 0.5 seconds when nothing has moved.

today: RFC 5826 is an Informational document from April 2010, and the metadata lists no replacement or update. It records requirements for the ROLL work and defines no protocol itself.

sections.title: Home Control on Lossy Networks
sections.content:
This document gives requirements specific to home control and automation for Routing Over Low power and Lossy (ROLL) networks. Homes will contain many wireless devices: actuators (relay, light dimmer, heating valve), sensors (wall switch, water leak, blood pressure) and controllers. A single node can be both, as with a wall switch that has a built-in relay.

Nodes have a limited radio range, so routing is often required. They are cheap, short of battery, memory and CPU, and work in unstable conditions: people moving, a door opening or a microwave oven starting can turn a good radio link bad for a while, which is why the networks are called lossy. All traffic in a ROLL network is carried as IPv6 packets.

The text focuses on radio but says it applies equally to other low-power links such as IEEE 802.15.4, Bluetooth, Low-Power WiFi and power-line communication. It overlaps with the industrial, urban and building requirements documents (RFC 5673, RFC 5548, and RFC 5867).
sections.eli5: Little gadgets in a house can only shout a short distance, so they pass messages along like kids in a line. The line has to cope with gadgets that sleep and with signals that come and go.

sections.title: Node Roles and Terms
sections.content:
The RFC defines a few node roles. An actuator performs a physical action, such as a dimmer or relay. A sensor measures a physical parameter or detects an event. A controller controls actuators, based on sensor readings, schedules or commands from the Internet. If sufficiently powered, any of the three may take part in routing.

A border router connects the ROLL network to the Internet or a backbone. Upstream means traffic from a Personal Area Network (PAN) to a LAN device, and downstream is the reverse. The RFC also defines Demand-Response (users adjusting consumption to power pricing) and Demand-Side Management (utilities enabling and disabling loads).
sections.eli5: Some gadgets sense things, some do things, and some are the boss. A border router is the front door that links the house network to the outside world.

sections.title: Home Automation Use Cases
sections.content:
Section 2 of the RFC lists typical applications. In lighting, one event such as leaving home may switch many lights off, and they should appear to turn off at the same time. For energy saving, appliances may be controlled by timers, sensors or pricing information. Mains-powered appliances are ideal always-on routers, while battery nodes are constrained.

A moving remote control must appear to react instantly, within a few hundred milliseconds. Adding a module needs an automated inclusion process (neighbor detection and a unique node ID) that should finish within a few seconds. Battery-powered window shades sleep most of the time, so a command may wait for the next wake-up. Other cases are video surveillance, which involves direct device-to-device communication, healthcare reporting and monitoring, and alarm systems.

For alarms, battery-powered safety devices such as smoke alarms should be used for routing only if no other option exists, and routing should avoid sleeping devices to keep delivery fast.
sections.eli5: Think of a house where one button can turn off every light, a remote can follow you from room to room, and a smoke alarm must shout at once. Each job needs the network to behave a certain way.

sections.title: The Routing Requirements
sections.content:
Section 3 turns the use cases into requirements.

  • Constraint-based routing: the protocol SHOULD route via mains-powered nodes if possible, and MUST support constraint-based routing that takes node properties into account (CPU, memory, energy level, sleep intervals, safety or convenience of changing a battery). Battery devices may need a duty cycle lower than 1%.
  • Mobility: a remote control appears unresponsive if it takes more than 0.5 seconds to pause the music, while healthcare devices can tolerate route discovery times of seconds.
  • Scalability: the protocol MUST support at least 250 devices and SHOULD be extensible beyond that.
  • Convergence time: it MUST converge within 0.5 seconds if no nodes have moved and within four seconds if nodes have moved. Here, converged means the originator has received a response from the destination, and the targets apply to up to 250 nodes with up to four repeating nodes between source and destination.
  • Manageability: the protocol MUST provide zero-configuration, so a node can obtain an address and join on its own.
  • Stability: a node that fails often SHOULD NOT be the first choice for routing.
sections.eli5: The chain of helper gadgets should prefer plugged-in helpers, let a moving remote keep working, grow to a few hundred gadgets, answer in a blink, set itself up, and stop trusting gadgets that keep failing.

sections.title: Traffic Patterns
sections.content:
Traffic depends on the design. In a distributed system, wall switches control lamps directly and traffic tends to be multipoint-to-multipoint. In a centralized system, switches talk to a central lighting computer and traffic is a mix of multipoint-to-point and point-to-multipoint.

Wall switches send traffic only when used, typically one to ten times per hour. Sensors report when queried or at fixed intervals, typically minutes. Motion sensors send a frame when motion starts and another after an idle period. Frames are short, typically less than five bytes of payload, and acknowledgment frames of a few bytes are used. Lost frames and interference can cause retransmissions.
sections.eli5: The gadgets mostly send tiny notes now and then, like a button press, and they get a tiny thank-you note back.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC notes that wireless, distributed and resource-constrained networks face routing security threats, and that security must be lightweight enough to run on every node. An attacker can snoop, replay or originate messages to disrupt routing.

The network MUST be able to authenticate a new node before it takes part in routing decisions, and the routing protocol MUST support message integrity. Routing protocols MUST support authentication and integrity, and SHOULD support confidentiality. They SHOULD defend against denial-of-service attacks. Damage SHOULD be commensurate with the number of nodes physically compromised, so taking over one node should not deny service to the whole network.

Because ease of use matters in homes and constant snooping is considered unlikely, the network key MAY be exposed for short periods while new nodes are included. Electronic door locks and other critical applications SHOULD add end-to-end application security.
sections.eli5: A new gadget must prove who it is before it joins, and one broken or hacked gadget should not knock out the whole house.
